paragraphs.title: The Vision of the Ram and the Goat

easy.explanation: Daniel was at Shushan in the palace, beside the river Ulai.
easy.q: Where was Daniel when he saw the vision?
How many horns did the ram have?

easy.explanation: When the goat became strong, its great horn was broken.
easy.q: What happened to the great horn of the goat?

medium.explanation: The ram pushed westward, northward, and southward.
medium.q: In which directions did the ram push?

medium.explanation: Four notable horns came up toward the four winds of heaven.
medium.q: What appeared in place of the broken great horn?
What does the word “notable” describe in the phrase “a notable horn”?

answers: No beast could stand before it or deliver from its hand
challenge.explanation: The ram acted according to its will, and no beast could stand before it.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the ram was powerful at first?

answers: It moved with great speed and force
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes the goat’s swift and powerful movement.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the goat coming “on the face of the whole earth, and touched not the ground”?

answers: Four horns appeared, and then the goat defeated the ram
The ram won, and then a great horn grew on it
The goat defeated the ram, its great horn was broken, and four horns appeared
challenge.explanation: The goat defeated the ram; afterward its great horn was broken and four horns arose.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events in the vision?

paragraphs.title: The Small Horn and Its Attack on the Holy

answers: From one of the four horns
easy.explanation: The little horn came forth from one of the four horns.
easy.q: From where did the little horn come?

answers: Toward the south, the east, and the pleasant land
easy.explanation: It grew toward the south, the east, and the pleasant land.
easy.q: Toward which places did the little horn grow?

easy.explanation: The answer says, “Unto two thousand and three hundred days.”
easy.q: How many days are mentioned in the answer to the vision?

answers: It cast some of them down and stamped upon them
medium.explanation: It cast some of the host and stars to the ground and stamped upon them.
medium.q: What did the little horn do to the host of heaven and the stars?

answers: The daily sacrifice and the place of the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The daily sacrifice was taken away, and the sanctuary was cast down.
medium.q: What was taken away or cast down by the little horn?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the heavenly host represented in the vision.
medium.q: In context, what does “the host of heaven” refer to?

answers: The horn grew powerful, and therefore it attacked the sacrifice and sanctuary
The truth grew strong, and therefore it was cast down
The sanctuary was rebuilt, and therefore the horn was broken
challenge.explanation: The horn’s growth and self-exaltation led to its attacks on the holy things.
challenge.q: Which cause-and-effect relationship is described in the passage?

answers: How long the desolation and trampling would continue
challenge.explanation: They asked how long the vision and the trampling of the sanctuary and host would last.
challenge.q: What did the saints ask to know?

answers: The sanctuary would ultimately be restored and made right
The sanctuary would be replaced by four horns
challenge.explanation: After the appointed period, the sanctuary would be cleansed.
challenge.q: What does the cleansing of the sanctuary indicate in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Angel Explains the Vision to Daniel

answers: A command to build a sanctuary
easy.explanation: Daniel sought for the meaning of the vision.
easy.q: What did Daniel seek after seeing the vision?

easy.explanation: A voice commanded Gabriel to make Daniel understand the vision.
easy.q: Who was commanded to make Daniel understand the vision?

answers: He was afraid and fell upon his face
easy.explanation: Daniel was afraid and fell upon his face.
easy.q: How did Daniel react when the angel came near?

answers: He touched Daniel and set him upright
He sent Daniel to the king
medium.explanation: The angel touched Daniel and set him upright.
medium.q: What did the angel do after Daniel fell?

medium.explanation: Gabriel said that the vision concerned the time of the end.
medium.q: What time does the vision concern according to the angel?

answers: Daniel sought understanding, and Gabriel was sent to explain
Daniel sought a kingdom, and Gabriel gave it to him
Daniel sought escape, and Gabriel stopped him
medium.explanation: Daniel sought the meaning, and Gabriel was commanded to explain the vision.
medium.q: What is the connection between Daniel’s request and Gabriel’s appearance?

answers: The vision was simple and unimportant
The vision caused fear and physical weakness
challenge.explanation: Daniel fell down, slept on his face, and later became sick.
challenge.q: What does Daniel’s reaction reveal about the power of the vision?

answers: The vision concerns a future appointed time of fulfillment
The vision concerns only that same day
The vision concerns only a particular place
challenge.explanation: The phrase points to a future time fixed by God.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the phrase “at the time appointed the end shall be”?

answers: He fell, sought understanding, and then saw the vision
He saw the vision, sought understanding, fell, and was set upright
He became sick, saw the vision, and then sought understanding
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence given in the passage.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Daniel’s actions?

paragraphs.title: The Meaning of the Ram, the Goat, and the Four Kingdoms

answers: The kings of Media and Persia
easy.explanation: The ram represents the kings of Media and Persia.
The rough goat represents the king of Grecia.
The four horns represent four kingdoms.
easy.q: What do the four horns represent?

medium.explanation: The great horn represents the first king.
medium.q: What does the great horn between the goat’s eyes represent?

answers: They would stand in their own strength
They would stand, but not in the power of the first king
They would become one horn again
medium.explanation: Four kingdoms would stand up, but not in the power of the first king.
medium.q: What would happen to the four kingdoms that arose after the great horn was broken?

answers: Realms or nations ruled by kings
medium.explanation: A kingdom is a realm or nation governed by a king.
medium.q: What does the word “kingdoms” mean in this passage?

answers: The four horns appeared before the great horn
The four horns appeared after the great horn was broken
The great horn grew out of the four horns
challenge.explanation: After the great horn was broken, four horns stood up in its place.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between the great horn and the four horns?

answers: They represent kingdoms arising from the nation of Greece
They belong only to the ram
They have no connection with kingdoms
challenge.explanation: The four kingdoms would stand up out of the nation of Greece.
challenge.q: What does the interpretation teach about the four horns and Greece?

answers: They would stand, but not in his power
They would have only one horn
They would appear beside the river Ulai
challenge.explanation: The passage expressly says they would not stand in the power of the first king.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes that the later kingdoms would not equal the first king in power?

paragraphs.title: The Fierce King and His Fall

easy.explanation: A king of fierce countenance and understanding dark sentences would arise.
easy.q: What kind of king would arise in the latter time?

answers: The mighty and the holy people
easy.explanation: He would destroy the mighty and the holy people.
He would be broken without hand.
easy.q: How would the king be broken?

medium.explanation: He would cause craft to prosper and destroy many by peace.
medium.q: By what means would the king prosper for a time?

medium.explanation: He would stand up against the Prince of princes.
medium.q: Against whom would the king stand?

answers: A bold, harsh, and threatening character
medium.explanation: The phrase describes someone bold, harsh, and threatening.
medium.q: What does “fierce countenance” suggest about the king?

answers: He prospers for a time, but is finally broken
He is weak at first and rules forever
He immediately submits and later conquers
challenge.explanation: Although he prospers for a time, he is ultimately broken.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in the king’s story?

answers: His power is not presented as originating from himself alone
He does not act at all
He is weaker than every person
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that his power comes from a source beyond himself.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the phrase “not by his own power”?

answers: He remained sick and never returned to work
He was sick for certain days, then rose and did the king’s business
challenge.explanation: Daniel fainted and was sick, but afterward he rose and did the king’s business.
challenge.q: What did Daniel do after the vision?
